Overview:
Take over as the teacher of twenty high school students as they attempt to find their way through life. Manage and develop relationships with each of them in the fictional city of Kumon-mi. Choose how to spend your time after school and on weekends to best suit the path you want to take. Whether it be visiting the girls at their part time jobs, trying to convince them to let you into their dorm rooms, or just hanging out in the room with clocks at the local bar, there is always something to do in Lessons in Love.
Please note, some things in this game may be meant to confuse or disturb you.
But don't worry! Everything will be okay~​

Overview:
Take over as the teacher of twenty high school students as they attempt to find their way through life. Manage and develop relationships with each of them in the fictional city of Kumon-mi. Choose how to spend your time after school and on weekends to best suit the path you want to take. Whether it be visiting the girls at their part time jobs, trying to convince them to let you into their dorm rooms, or just hanging out in the room with clocks at the local bar, there is always something to do in Lessons in Love.
Please note, some things in this game may be meant to confuse or disturb you.
But don't worry! Everything will be okay~​

I had a bit of fun based on the expansion pack lines.

A World Without Bubbles
It's been ten years now since that cursed day...

The day my beautiful wife and the only light in my life was killed in a bubble wrap accident. Since then I've dedicated myself to improving shipping packaging, and I've found unprecedented economic success.

Why is it, then, that I still feel so empty?

I barely see my daughter... she lives at her school in the city. I wonder if she still thinks of me as her father. Perhaps Geoffrey would know how she feels, he seems close to her.

I've done my best to use my fortune to support those close to me.
It's a little unfair to say that, though, as I don't feel close to anyone.

I need something to wake me from this lack of life.

*ring* *ring*
"Yes... I see... Ah. I'll have someone from R&D take a look on Monday."
That's right, this is what I do now...

Even on the weekends my life is consumed by my packaging empire. At least I've finally rid the world of the poppable bubble wrap that killed my wife. Maybe that's enough for one man. But is this empty life really what I want?
A World Without Geoffrey's Family
I wonder if the master of this house will ever notice how I look at him? I still remember the day I got the news about my family.

He took me in to his powerful arms, brought his beautiful lips to my head and whispered,
"Don't worry Geoffrey. I'll take care of you."

The next day he went about his business as if nothing had happened. How long can I keep going forward with these feelings in my heart?

Oh master, you were there when the void in my heart was at it's largest, and now it's so full of you it feels like it's at risk of bursting. What can I do to make you notice how I feel?
Selebus, did you know about Geoffrey's feelings?

That bit of silly fun aside, this seems like a wonderful project and if you need any help with skills in my wheelhouse (see: Adobe Photoshop, English writing, relatively basic coding (Javascript, Python) I'd love to help out. One thing I'm relatively competent at is adding cum to images. A quick example that only took a few minutes (other styles are also no problem):
No worries if not, but this project definitely looks fun.

Minor continuity issue
First time going to bar is on a Monday
"Ami won't mind if I stay out a little late since it's the weekend"
in SanaEvents.rpy

spoilers.text:
It's been ten years now since that cursed day...
The day my beautiful wife and the only light in my life was killed in a bubble wrap accident. Since then I've dedicated myself to improving shipping packaging, and I've found unprecedented economic success.
Why is it, then, that I still feel so empty?
I barely see my daughter... she lives at her school in the city. I wonder if she still thinks of me as her father. Perhaps Geoffrey would know how she feels, he seems close to her.
I've done my best to use my fortune to support those close to me.
It's a little unfair to say that, though, as I don't feel close to anyone.
I need something to wake me from this lack of life.
*ring* *ring*
"Yes... I see... Ah. I'll have someone from R&D take a look on Monday."
That's right, this is what I do now...
Even on the weekends my life is consumed by my packaging empire. At least I've finally rid the world of the poppable bubble wrap that killed my wife. Maybe that's enough for one man. But is this empty life really what I want?

spoilers.html:
I wonder if the master of this house will ever notice how I look at him? I still remember the day I got the news about my family.

He took me in to his powerful arms, brought his beautiful lips to my head and whispered,
"Don't worry Geoffrey. I'll take care of you."

The next day he went about his business as if nothing had happened. How long can I keep going forward with these feelings in my heart?

Oh master, you were there when the void in my heart was at it's largest, and now it's so full of you it feels like it's at risk of bursting. What can I do to make you notice how I feel?

I enjoyed the game quite a lot.

The characters seem interesting enough, each one with their own discerning quirks but not as simple as they might seem, I'm interested in exploring their stories, way more than I am interested in the h-scenes, which is good, it means I'm enjoying the plot.

Some questions I have for the Dev:

-How complete is the game at the moment? I know this is just the first release but I still spent like 2-3 hours playing, I wonder how long it will be once it is complete.

- Are you planning on doing different endings? or is it going to be linear? after all there are "choices" to spend time with different girls but if we have an infinite time, we are able to eventually unlock all the scenes in a single playthrough.

- This one more or less links with my second question, Do we have finite time? to unlock all the scenes possible, I spent around 40 in-game days, but if I'm able to just do that, wouldn't it be too easy? though that is my opinion, I know it is not that kind of hardcore game in which you have to do everything perfectly to get the happy/harem ending...

- There is this spacial war or whatever it is going on, I wonder if you are going to implement more of it into the story or if it is just background information to give a reason as to why there are so few males in the city? tbh it gave me some Mu-Luv vibes, when it was first just a cute school-setting eroge but then you are introduced into the REAL GAME.

- Are there any other elements you are planning to introduced? so far there is the "Affection/love meter", choices, and "time management" with the daily events. As a teacher you receive a salary so I wonder if we will eventually have a shop or events that require certain amount of money. stuff like that. tho if you think you can't or that would be too much work, is better not make the scope of the game so big that it becomes unbearable for you. Many others have failed because the expectations were too much for the developer to handle.

Now I wanna give my opinion about each girl...

Not much to say about her, tbh she seems like the most simple character of the bunch, well, besides being in love with her uncle. I wonder what kind of backstory she will have, if she is a yandere, then she probably murdered her parents to be alone with her uncle...though that is unlikely, although she seems to be the kind to manipulate him in secret.

This one interests me the most... At first I though she might be a closet chunnibyou because of the scene in the Shrine, but "that room" made me change the evaluation I had about her. I have no idea now.

Well not much to say about her, the open pervert of the bunch. tho I thought she was going to be the dominating type because of her upbringing.

This is my favorite so far, dunno, I have always been into this kind of girl. Though she seems like a tough nut to crack. I wonder what her backstory is? She seems like the type to either have a really tough childhood or a really good one but as the daughter of a Yakuza family...I wonder which it will be.

She was surprising, I though it was gonna be the typical gyaru type but nope. Hopefully you will be able to properly develop her character.

Well this one obviously is in love with the teacher, and because she is the more "straight" one of all of them, I bet she will have the most hardcore h-scenes... Although I can't see what direction her character development will take. I like her personality and all but...since playing Katawa Shoujo (my first vn), I always initially hate the characters that look like and have a similar role as Shizune.

One of the two, she either has a dick or she is an extreme yandere. Maybe both.

Not much to say about her, she is the athletic one....

NECROMANCER!!!! her character design, style, and decoraction of the room screams NECROMANCER at your face. Dunno, the world setting is weird so everything is possible LOL. Jokes aside, she is my second favorite.

Tbh I don't know. She seems like the simple shy girl. not much to say about her.

Now I wanna talk about the room with clocks....

I already knew what was coming, because I read the comments in this post before I found the room with clocks, but still freaked me a bit, I was a bit scared during the whole event. Though it didn't helped that I was playing at 3 am with all the lights on my room off.

If I'm not wrong, the character in that room is Maya, which is why it made me change my opinion on her... The room is full of clocks, but the clocks do not have hands, which makes me think of either a time stop or an infinite time. There is also the possibility of her being stuck in a time loop which is why she knew instantly why Sensei isn't the same as always.

Also correct if I'm wrong, but the beeps in the room is morse code. I'm gonna try to confirm it though it is quite hard since I have no fucking idea how to read morse code. The beeps keep looping along with the lullaby. once the lullaby starts from the beginning, the beeps also start then.

Overall it was a good first release, I'm showing interest in support you through patreon (tho that would be next month).
Good luck.

posts.content_html_raw:
Vidashall said:
How complete is the game at the moment?
Click to expand...
Nowhere near finished! And if the subsequent builds are close in length to the initial one (Which I imagine they should be), we're looking at over doubling the current length before all of the dorm rooms are even open. The way I'm structuring the game leaves a lot of room for it to sort of 'keep going.' Sure, there's an underlying 'main' plot line, but I'm hoping the girls' individual stories are what wind up keeping everyone coming back at the end of the day- and there are already ten of those I'm in the process of writing.

Vidashall said:
Are you planning on doing different endings? or is it going to be linear?
Click to expand...
As of right now, time is not finite. I'd like for the main plot and all subplots to work in tandem with one another so everyone can see everything the game has to offer. This doesn't mean, though, that everything will be linear in terms of an ending. Whenever the game does end (In the far, far future), your standing with certain girls will have some sort of impact. I've also toyed with another idea I'd like to explore in that regard, but I won't divulge any more information about that until I'm certain it can be done.

Vidashall said:
There is this spacial war or whatever it is going on, I wonder if you are going to implement more of it into the story or if it is just background information
Click to expand...
That's a tricky question to answer, especially since you brought up Muv Luv. As of right now, I can't say that the whole war thing is going to get even half as crazy as ML, but it will come into play in some form or another.

Vidashall said:
Are there any other elements you are planning to introduced?
Click to expand...
Yes! There are other systems and stats I'd like to introduce eventually, but I'd like to refine and perfect the ones we have now first. I know there are a couple stretch goals on the Patreon page that I set as sort of landmarks for telling myself "Okay, we all want this" but, like I said, I'm focusing more on what we have now at the moment.

Sidenote: I will confirm that the beeps are not morse code, but there may be some sort of other message hidden in them.

posts.content_html_raw:
Edit: Sorry for the wall of text!

Man this game is so damn good. I usually come and play games like these to have my fill, but every now and then a game comes along that has amazing writing. Even rarer though, is when a work of art comes along with good writing AND this sense of being genuine where it feels like the pacing is good and the interactions between characters don't make you go "this feels a little too forced" or makes you ask yourself "why these dialogue choices?"; where it makes you feel a deeper sense of duty to pay attention to the story and everything surrounding it without feeling like you're going out of your way to do so. Even more, it feels like you pay attention to details, which makes it all the more genuine. For instance, the fact each girl both lines up with their image, backstory, and even their actions is great, but on top of all of that you have them doing little things like Yumi attending class and counseling more as you get closer to her even early on. Then there's something like Akane having a chicken in class and it not even being addressed because she's just wild and unpredictable by nature. You blend that mix of showing not telling and actually showing really well and then when I get to thinking "Oh the author slipped up!," and I think I've caught you in some type of continuity error or something related, you explain it off as a wall break. You're a good writer fam. My favorite character so far has to be Futaba, and I imagine that you also enjoy writing her as she had the most scenes (at least the most revealing ((as in her characterization)) and how she's the most built upon). I gotta say you caught me off guard a lot of times too. The worst time was the "There's something buried underneath the school." It caught me so off guard I was kind of stuck in place out of fear. It got me curious with the notebook you and Futaba read as the mysterious owner of it mentions how the school's boiler room smells of "rotten skin flesh," if I recall correctly. Then Futaba also has that quote by Edgar Allen Poe from the beginning of the game. I wonder how it's all connected. I'm sorry for the long wall of text, but damn this work of art is just off to too much of a good start not to rant on it. I'll try to join your patreon asap. With what's going on I've been in a difficult place but your game definitely was a gem in all of it. I hope you're doing alright through recent events and thanks for the game, it's awesome. Much love fam.

Space war... i could read a spin off about a mc having fun the female soldiers on one of those ships.. just saying.
My head is already making its own theories and triying to guess how some of the girls are gonna fall for the mc and that is something that doesnt happen very often to me with VN.

In short.. amazing writing that makes me forget this is F95 and the original plan was to just fap to this.

Realized it would be weird for a bunch of students to be running around calling their teacher by his first name, especially your niece who is supposed to know your real name. Sensei’s also a lot less of a self-insert character than originally intended, so fully naming him feels off.

HOWEVER, I do think I’ll be able to assign custom master/sex-names for every girl that they’ll use during h-scenes and some other events. These will be chosen during specific segments of their stories, so we’ll if it makes sense to have any in the next update. Ideally, I’d like to start including those soon, just want it to be done in believable fashion.

Because if so, that was more of a joke about the public crucifixion of Jesus rather than commentary on crucifixion as a whole.
Click to expand...
But the whole POINT of executions, at least until Modern Times, was to be a deterrent, so they usually WERE public.

As for suffocation (probably more properly asphyxiation), probably none of the cultures that used crucifixion (mainly Rome in the Classical Period and Shoganate Japan) realized what the actual cause of death was. That knowledge had to wait until a reasonably modern understanding of Anatomy and Bodily Functions. (None of the ancient civilizations realized the actual purpose of Respiration, for instance.) Of all the ancient physicians, perhaps only Galen might have been able to figure it out, and if I recall correctly, his time was after crucifixion ceased to be the main form of execution for the Romans.

I just finished my first play through and I'm struggling to figure it out. I have a few theories though.
1. The MC is in the midst of an extreme psychotic break and the only real person (maybe the only person that can still partially get through to him) is Maya or Maya is a representation of the last string of rationality he's holding onto.
2. They're all dead and in some form of simulated reality/purgatory/whatever and Maya is the only one aware of the truth or an observer/god like being. Or maybe the third secret event actually happened and she blames the MC?
3. They're all patients in an asylum and are in some trial virtual/simulated reality treatment. Maya may be a nurse or she somehow knows the truth.
Let's go full on creepy with the next two.
4. The MC is crazy, kidnapped all the girls, broke their minds/brainwashed them and is living out a fantasy. Alternatively some third party could have kidnapped them all, brainwashed/broken them and is watching them.
5. The MC had a full blown psychotic break, killed all of the girls and turned them into human puppets and is now living out his harem fantasy with those puppets (Yes. That would mean sex with...).

Whatever it actually turns out to be is sure to be some complete mind fuck and a huge emotional rollercoaster, so I both love and hate you Selebus. Just to clarify. I love you for what appears to be an engaging story, but also hate you for it due to the creepy and unpleasant aspects (it's so much harder to enjoy the good stuff when you realize there's something seriously wrong beneath the surface). The stat grinding is a bit annoying though, given you have to wait for the weekends for some of the stuff. I'll definitely be back though.
P.S. Rin is my favourite and I hate you for what you did to her (made me sad).

posts.content_html_raw:
ANDROID PLAYERS: There is an official port now, so you may need to transfer your saves as the APK is different. I don't have an Android device, but a kind soul from the LiL Discord has provided these instructions for anyone requiring assistance with this.

1. Open up the new Ren'py port to create a file path.
2. Most phones should have a "files" app, if not, most free ones on the app store will work perfectly fine. From there, open up your internal storage, once it's open, click on the folder labeled "Android", then "data".
3. You're gonna see a ton of folders labeled "com.name", you're going to look for the one that's labeled as "ll_androidmo.me". Once you have found that folder, open it, click on "files" and now you should see a folder labeled "saves". That houses all your manual, and auto saves. Copy (or cut) the folder by holding down on it and selecting the option.
4. Go back to the "data" folder that has all the "com." folders, now locate the one labeled as "com.selebus.lil040". Go into the "files" folder and paste the save folder in. If it asks you to replace, that's perfectly fine.
5. Close out of the renpy port of LiL and reopen.
6. Once you verify your saves have been ported over, the old app can be deleted.
posts.content_text_full:
ANDROID PLAYERS:
There is an official port now, so you may need to transfer your saves as the APK is different. I don't have an Android device, but a kind soul from the LiL Discord has provided these instructions for anyone requiring assistance with this.
Spoiler:
Transferring saves on Android
1. Open up the new Ren'py port to create a file path.
2. Most phones should have a "files" app, if not, most free ones on the app store will work perfectly fine. From there, open up your internal storage, once it's open, click on the folder labeled "Android", then "data".
3. You're gonna see a ton of folders labeled "com.name", you're going to look for the one that's labeled as "ll_androidmo.me". Once you have found that folder, open it, click on "files" and now you should see a folder labeled "saves". That houses all your manual, and auto saves. Copy (or cut) the folder by holding down on it and selecting the option.
4. Go back to the "data" folder that has all the "com." folders, now locate the one labeled as "com.selebus.lil040". Go into the "files" folder and paste the save folder in. If it asks you to replace, that's perfectly fine.
5. Close out of the renpy port of LiL and reopen.
6. Once you verify your saves have been ported over, the old app can be deleted.

posts.content_html_raw:
Congrats Selebus, you have the rare honour of getting me to play the entire game without even masturbating once. Sheesh, I don't know whether to be content or angry. All I wanted was to play a porn game for an hour last Thursday and then play some more The Witness, and instead I ended up getting sucked into the game's story and writing and I spent 9 hours Thursday and Friday uncovering all of the content there was to find.

One area I do need to specifically commend you on though in regards to the generally excellent writing is the game's intro. In general terms most indie porn games, and even indie visual novels from which I think you've said you've taking more inspiration from, no matter the actual quality of the game either drop you right in the middle of things or have a bog-standard, rather lacklustre intro.
And that's a shame. Because if the game is mediocre or crap that's just par for the course, to be expected. But sometimes there are actually good games with good plots out there, and lots of people don't get past the first 10 minutes of it because the intro is not indicative of what the actual game is like.

And so I'm glad to see you've avoided falling into this trap with the intro you have here. You managed to lean onto the hidden darkness, the troubling depths beyond the surface that arise in certain parts of the game if you look for them, to have a hook to grab the player and keep them engaged beyond just "quickly checking it out". You have the ominous references to escapism, the "this world was made for you" message, the multiple "jump" commands, and then the very frantic, almost glitching intro screen. It definitely manages to get the impression across that something's not right here.
And yet it's also balanced well enough that it doesn't scare people off, or overwhelms the player, for it might just be a rather quirky intro by an indie dev talking about escapism. Add in the well-chosen background music (haven't seen anyone comment on this yet which is weird, as I find the music choice, especially in the secret scenes, to be very appropriate to the ongoing narrative) and it's a great intro to a, so far, great game.

I want to give some feedback playing the game as a first-timer in 0.5.0, how long it took me and my general playstyle and impressions and all, but I'll do it in a collapsible so as to not fill people's screens with a wall of text beyond what I've already written.

So, first of all some general stats.

It took me around 9 hours to get through all the available content so far, and I didn't miss a single scene according to the event tracker. This includes getting Ami, Ayane, Futaba, Makoto, and Sara all up to 5 lust. It took me 176 in-game days to achieve this, though I definitely believe this can be done faster with proper optimisation once you have some knowledge of how the game works.

I did play somewhat... strategic, I think would be the best word. At first I started off only spending time with Ami, Ayane, and Maya since they were the first girls to be introduced and I went in with the mentality of "getting them out of the way", as it were. But once I realised that you could also level affection by spending time with the girls at the dorms I instead spent my weekends hanging out with girls specifically to get the girls with low affection up to 5 as fast as I could, since this opened up possibilities to increase their affection every day of the week rather than visit the bar or porn shop at night. Similarly I would also choose these girls after school in the dorms in they were hanging out in the hallway for the same reason.

The same thing happened when I realised new events usually trigger at affection levels in multiple of fives, just trying to level as many girls to these levels as I could so I had the possibility to trigger their next scene in the weekend events if that happened to be the case.

This resulted in me having a generally steady flow of content up until about 2/3rds into the game. Every week I had usually around 2-3 main story or girl-specific events triggering, meaning I never really felt "bored" or that I was grinding. Of course eventually the main story events started to slow down as more and more of them got locked behind girl-specific events, and I was completing some girls meaning my events with them were stopping as well, meaning I had less avenues of content. This was around in-game day 90 I think, and around day 120 I was full-on holding SHIFT most of the time just to speed through the text and grind stats until I got a new event.

In terms of the order in which I pursued the girls I started off with Ami, Ayane, and Maya as I mentioned, since they were the first girls to be introduced. But I quickly stopped chasing Maya after her first shrine event, since I realised that with her knowing the character is not the real Sensei, on top of her dialogue in other Ami scenes, she is probably more connected to the whole darker plot lurking in the background (the Room with Clocks helped solidify this impression as well) and I wanted to leave that for last.
This is also why I left Yumi for last as well, since her first proper event happened in the Other Side of Town and had Sensei having very intrusive thoughts about murder and ended up molesting the poor girl, even thinking about raping her, with his body unable to resist or even speak what he wanted. This, combined with the fact that she reacted the most realistic of all the girls about a teacher coming on to their students, even commenting on how weird it was that everyone else seems to think this is fine, made me think that she was going to be connected to this hidden underbelly of the story as well. Though given her recent scenes warming up to Sensei with the job hunt haven't proven my suspicions right here.

After dropping Maya and Yumi I focussed on Ami and Aya, with Makoto and Sana as well, simply because I could visit them at night every day in the bar and porn shop, making them easily accessible. Then followed Chika and Futaba, since they were characters that had made an impact in the story thus far, and finally Miku and Rin. This, yes, meant that I was missing the "Missing" event for quite a while as well. Honestly I even started to think that maybe this event was missing on purpose, like as part of the game's darker narrative this was an event that happened off-screen and the characters know about, but Sensei had forgotten and the player wasn't privy to, much like that time Sensei zoned out for 10 minutes wandering around in one of Yumi's events, and that the only hint towards this event happening would be its inclusion in the event tracker.

Given that you've mentioned this event triggers late for a lot of people it could indicate that Rin is on average focussed on later than the other characters, and I think this might be because early in the game there's nothing that really makes her stand out. Same with Miku. Ami has the benefit of being the first character the player meets, and is Sensei's family. Ayane is similarly friends was Ami, shows up a lot, and already has affection towards Sensei to start off with. Idem for Maya. Makoto and Sana are easily accessible at the start of the game, not locked behind weekend events since they are available every night, and Makoto has an early scene showcasing her character on top of this. Futaba and Yumi have the bullying-scene reasonably early in the game, giving the player a small introduction to their character. And even Chika has the small scene at the very start where she leaves class to listen to a radio show, giving her some personality (also, has anyone commented on the LiSA reference yet? I can't be the first one, right?). But Rin and Miku seem to lack a certain intro at the start to properly cement their character in the player's mind (and if they have one I can't remember it, which is part of the issue then I guess), which could be why people tend to explore them later than other characters.

That all aside, let me focus on the characters I enjoy the most. Now since I'm a whore for character development and interaction, at the top are by a large margin Maya, Yumi, and, ironically, Rin. Simply because they have a lot of unique scenes in their story already, as well as interesting interactions with Sensei. Then come Makoto and Chika, since they have a nice gradual buildup with the whole porn-shop and little sister angle, and even though it hasn't been built up as much as the other three stories they still have a fair bit of story to them I enjoy a lot.
Next are Sana and Futaba, because even if they have a fair bit of story to them so far both of them have been rather cliché. Making a shy girl come out of her shell and helping a girl with a negative self-image who likes books coming to terms with the fact that her body is fine and aiding her writing, it's all pretty stereotypical so far. I've no doubt their more unique personalities will shine through in the future, given the fact that Sana for one seems baffled by the fact that Sensei is talking about "affection scores not being high enough" and telling her to become friends with the entire class "because that's what always happens" while she's more than happy with just a few friends.
And then at the bottom we have Ami, Ayane, and Miku. Miku because so far relatively little has happened, safe for her freak-out in the storage shed, and Ami and Ayane because, since they started off already in love with Sensei, they've had little chance for change or development so far. Ami's trip to her parent's grave is the sole stand-out on her story so far in my mind, as even the karaoke and food contest are just extension of her personality that we've already seen in the first few minutes of the game. Same for Ayane.
But these are my personal opinion, and I've no doubt many people will have completely different opinions and favourites than mine, so feel free to completely disregard what I've just said.

I've also encountered one typo and a bug, so I wanted to draw attention to that as well.


This line, after having had sex with Sara, should say "having had sex with her mom" rather than "having sex with her mom", I think.

The bug then was right after Rin's scene in the cafe following her doctor's visit, where she was sent home for not being in any state to work. After getting this scene on Sunday morning I visited her in the dorms at night, and after knocking on her door, meaning to check up on her, I was instead able to spent some time hanging out with her with her looking right as rain just as usual, only for the "Missing" event to trigger first thing on Monday with Futaba saying Rin is skipping school due to circumstances. Now I'm pretty sure the player shouldn't be able to visit regular happy-go-lucky Rin in between these events like I did.

Anyhow that's all I have to say so far (and that was a lot, sheesh), except to thank you for the great game you've made so far. I immediately went to subscribe on Patreon after finishing all available content on Friday, since I really want you to be able to tell the rest of the story you have in mind. Hope you have a great day, and that my ramblings were even somewhat interesting!

This, combined with the fact that she reacted the most realistic of all the girls about a teacher coming on to their students, even commenting on how weird it was that everyone else seems to think this is fine, made me think that she was going to be connected to this hidden underbelly of the story as well. Though given her recent scenes warming up to Sensei with the job hunt haven't proven my suspicions right here.

After dropping Maya and Yumi I focussed on Ami and Aya, with Makoto and Sana as well, simply because I could visit them at night every day in the bar and porn shop, making them easily accessible. Then followed Chika and Futaba, since they were characters that had made an impact in the story thus far, and finally Miku and Rin. This, yes, meant that I was missing the "Missing" event for quite a while as well. Honestly I even started to think that maybe this event was missing on purpose, like as part of the game's darker narrative this was an event that happened off-screen and the characters know about, but Sensei had forgotten and the player wasn't privy to, much like that time Sensei zoned out for 10 minutes wandering around in one of Yumi's events, and that the only hint towards this event happening would be its inclusion in the event tracker.

Given that you've mentioned this event triggers late for a lot of people it could indicate that Rin is on average focussed on later than the other characters, and I think this might be because early in the game there's nothing that really makes her stand out. Same with Miku. Ami has the benefit of being the first character the player meets, and is Sensei's family. Ayane is similarly friends was Ami, shows up a lot, and already has affection towards Sensei to start off with. Idem for Maya. Makoto and Sana are easily accessible at the start of the game, not locked behind weekend events since they are available every night, and Makoto has an early scene showcasing her character on top of this. Futaba and Yumi have the bullying-scene reasonably early in the game, giving the player a small introduction to their character. And even Chika has the small scene at the very start where she leaves class to listen to a radio show, giving her some personality (also, has anyone commented on the LiSA reference yet? I can't be the first one, right?). But Rin and Miku seem to lack a certain intro at the start to properly cement their character in the player's mind (and if they have one I can't remember it, which is part of the issue then I guess), which could be why people tend to explore them later than other characters.

That all aside, let me focus on the characters I enjoy the most. Now since I'm a whore for character development and interaction, at the top are by a large margin Maya, Yumi, and, ironically, Rin. Simply because they have a lot of unique scenes in their story already, as well as interesting interactions with Sensei. Then come Makoto and Chika, since they have a nice gradual buildup with the whole porn-shop and little sister angle, and even though it hasn't been built up as much as the other three stories they still have a fair bit of story to them I enjoy a lot.
Next are Sana and Futaba, because even if they have a fair bit of story to them so far both of them have been rather cliché. Making a shy girl come out of her shell and helping a girl with a negative self-image who likes books coming to terms with the fact that her body is fine and aiding her writing, it's all pretty stereotypical so far. I've no doubt their more unique personalities will shine through in the future, given the fact that Sana for one seems baffled by the fact that Sensei is talking about "affection scores not being high enough" and telling her to become friends with the entire class "because that's what always happens" while she's more than happy with just a few friends.
And then at the bottom we have Ami, Ayane, and Miku. Miku because so far relatively little has happened, safe for her freak-out in the storage shed, and Ami and Ayane because, since they started off already in love with Sensei, they've had little chance for change or development so far. Ami's trip to her parent's grave is the sole stand-out on her story so far in my mind, as even the karaoke and food contest are just extension of her personality that we've already seen in the first few minutes of the game. Same for Ayane.
But these are my personal opinion, and I've no doubt many people will have completely different opinions and favourites than mine, so feel free to completely disregard what I've just said.

This line, after having had sex with Sara, should say "having had sex with her mom" rather than "having sex with her mom", I think.

The bug then was right after Rin's scene in the cafe following her doctor's visit, where she was sent home for not being in any state to work. After getting this scene on Sunday morning I visited her in the dorms at night, and after knocking on her door, meaning to check up on her, I was instead able to spent some time hanging out with her with her looking right as rain just as usual, only for the "Missing" event to trigger first thing on Monday with Futaba saying Rin is skipping school due to circumstances. Now I'm pretty sure the player shouldn't be able to visit regular happy-go-lucky Rin in between these events like I did.

Ironically managed to do exactly that in my playthrough as well. That is a big complication with a game like this, there are so many scenes lined up that you can easily get things that sound a bit inconsistent in context, but are fine as long as you understand that each scene is its own individual entity.

Also, hello there, haven't really spoken here before as I have been playing catch-up through the various released content. It hasn't been too long, since the beginning of July or so, but I have definitely enjoyed getting more acquainted with Nothing is Beautiful as well as this title. I am a bit of a VN fan, specifically with darker elements, and have enjoyed such things as Kara no Shoujo. I eventually hit a point where I realized a lot of Japanese VNs aren't translated, which in turn started distressing me since I felt like I was missing chapters from a larger story, which in turn made me start searching out English VNs. Since I preferred ones with adult elements, I thought this site would be good to find what I sought, but I ran across a lot of... mundane content that made me question if I made the right choice. Well, after looking under the horror tag and running across this title, it has definitely allured me.

Needless to say, I am not exactly the normal person here. Most came for the girls, stayed for the horror, I came for the horror and fell in love with the comedy and stories. This game is definitely one of the best VNs I know, mainly because of the ties to English. I definitely see what people mean by this game being somewhat similar to Doki Doki. The resetting of the world probably didn't help things there, plus it is what people think of when they think glitchy content. If I had to compare the two, I would say this game works a bit better, even with the horror element. Doki Doki had some flickering and suicidal scenes, but it never had things like Yumi's park scene or MS paint insanity.

The hidden scenes aren't just little surprises, they are some of the biggest attractions for me. They feel like a great period where you can let your creativity free and just let insanity in the door. It gets intriguing just how wild you will make the scenes and what exactly is going to occur. So far they have been quite nice to blunder across; so far I have naturally worked the routes in such a way that the scenes happened to occur when you least expected them. I will say that the new one for 5.0 is perhaps one of the best yet; it gave me a Cartagra vibe in what I felt was one of the best sequences of the game (Takako route).

Of course, the big thing of 5.0 is the words "everything is connected". After running through all the content, it is more true than ever, and I am quite glad I did things in the manner I did them. Perhaps it was just a side nod to Nothing is Beautiful... but what if it was something more? What if Yuu is Sensei? All paths intertwined. A million memories in the same place. What if this is Yuu's chance to live... a life that could be lived simply by jumping. A life where you no longer had to take candy or stay in the same place. A life where things are buried under the school and nobody looks for them because everybody is happy.

If I had to say a route I particularly am interested in, which is hard given that this game so far has you working all routes sort of simultaneously, I would say Yumi. It is probably the furthest interest from love I would have, since I absolutely dislike tsunderes and get more aggressive towards them (is it wrong that I cheered her being traumatized? Probably. But nothing is real). However, her reactions to Sensei following her around everywhere and the impromptu ska music works rather well. It makes it a rather fun read, even if I hate her as a person. I bet you hate many people too. All those people will be dead one day. You likely will be dead by then as well though.

Based on my tastes, I should probably be leaning towards the Sana route. The quiet shy character always seems alluring to me, perhaps because I am rather introverted. The leaning to escapism to avoid pain, the dissolution of the tangible threads around you as you embrace worlds far more interesting. If nothing is real, everything is equally relative, and thus all worlds are worlds to experience and place value in. However, she seems somewhat lacking in embracing darkness, instead playing Animal Crossing and seeking to improve herself.

Rin has that darkness I prefer, though she is far more punk rock than gothic or metal like I rather. She is also extremely social in ways that almost seem exhausting if done for too long. She could be a good wing-man though and a somewhat good friend. She seems genuinely interested in trying to get me with where I should be, so I must say that is a pretty welcoming quality to have in a friend. Plus being bisexual means that she can gauge my interests more, needed for a proper wingman.

Ayane isn't really a character I can say is attractive physically. Never been one for blonde hair. She manages to overcome this handicap with eccentric tastes that intrigue me, I enjoy the unpredictable and thus it is quite appealing to see what she will pull up. Plus we are on F95, someone that willingly is that perverted is a massive plus. Not sure how I feel about her tastes on pop music, but at least there is one girl who would willingly do anything sexual.

Ami just reminds me of Emi from Katawa Shoujo. Not only does she have a similar name and have a similar extroverted personality, but she also has dead parents. She, like the clone of her before her, fall into the category of being somewhat alright while also being nothing standout. Maybe Ami should do something different like murder someone. Maybe she should murder all the other girls and then finger herself to their corpses? Much better than just being a girl with dead parents.

Makoto is quite the competition for Ami in the "I don't really hate you but also don't really care you exist" category. It is a category reserved for most people and thus is one that isn't really that special or interesting. Thus I wouldn't be surprised if I was in a similar category for most people! She is supposed to be head over heels for me, but struggled to even give me a handjob in a porn shop. Ayane is making her look bad. Can we do trade-ins for my harem? I would like to find some other random person from another world and bring them here. We should be able to do that, after all I was born like that. Since morality is out of the window, why not mentally kidnap them and bring them to a city with no escape due to a space war? Then I could raise my affection ratings with them and we could totally remove Makoto from the world.

So thus we come to Miku. She has some trauma with loud noises, obviously PTSD from the war. Other than that, we haven't really seen much, outside of her trying to get me involved with two other random side girls and trying to convince me to caress the thighs of a bunch of high school girls. You know, I might actually like her as a wing-man better than Rin. Sure, she might not be bisexual, but she has done what Rin has yet to do. Get results. Can Rin hope to compete with Miku's small potential side harem to my main harem? Time will tell in Lessons in Love, an adult simulation game made by Selebus. For just $5, you can see Rin's imaginary side harem early. Or maybe you won't! That is the magic of this game. Just head over to patreon.com/lessonsinlove and show your support.

Chika is someone that is a decent person, but someone I hold absolutely no interest in whatsoever. Her style, her mannerisms, nothing about her says anything that I would really be interested in. I can imagine someone else might like her, but I am not too big a fan. I don't hate her, she is nice enough that I can accept her existing for the time being, but I also don't really hold much that is really compelling me to spend more time with her other than exploring all the content the game has to offer.

I hate Futaba. If there is someone I despise, it is her, and for that I can appreciate Yumi hating her even if Yumi also hates me. Maybe if Sensei would stop protecting Futaba, Yumi would stop hating him as much. Why do I hate Futaba so much, one might ask. Well, for starters, she is Yuri from Doki Doki. She might be a bit "fatter", though honestly my impressions of real people are that they are so gargantuan that even Futaba is nowhere near "fat". Half the time I forget that is even a characteristic of her. All of the time I hate her for being the silent bookworm with little self-confidence. I hate how one of her scenes involved mentioning dragons, one of my least favorite fictional animals. Cyclops are more interesting, much better than oversized dinosaurs that breathe fire and expect everyone to shower them with praise. I will hate Futaba more if she turns out to be a dragon. I once knew a dragon with big tits, absolutely terrible individual and I wouldn't expect Futaba to be any less evil than this dragon. I knew a real life person like Futaba once, someone who lacked self-confidence. Someone who pretended to fall in love. Someone who studied poems and quoted things. They took $5 from me and I never forgot it. That was $5 I could have used to be a Patreon member. I therefore cannot support this game because ghost-Futaba ripped me off and is now mocking me by being part of what that $5 would have been used for. She may pretend to be weak and lack confidence, but trust me when I say that she will wait for the worst time to steal money from you like the succubus she is. I have experienced many Futabas in the world. All of them end up leaving you because "you are too mentally ill" and accuse me of "assuming I am like a series of random fictional characters that you put through mental gymnastics to be like someone you can't get over". Futabas are everywhere. I see Futabas when I sleep, when I walk down the street, when I am trying to play visual novels to escape the pain of having Futabas around me. They don't want you to see them, but they are there, waiting for you to hand them $5. I know none of this will likely be justifiable reasons to hate Futaba, nobody can experience the things I have experienced. I know this will only cause Futabas to realize I am on to their cult and cause me to be further hated. But I had to explain this in the sliver of hope that I could find the non-Futaba who would agree with me and tell me "You know, she always was a manipulative bitch. Yumi may be insulting, but at least she is direct and honest about how much she hates me." Then I would look at them and be like "Yeah, we should totally form a I Hate Futaba fan club. I just suck at making T-Shirts, so hopefully you are good at graphic design." and they would be like "Eh, not really, but I got plenty of pictures of me sexually molesting my pregnant cat that we can use instead." I know it is a foolish dream to have, but perhaps one day we can live in a world where we have a I Hate Futaba fan club.

Maya is a normal teenage girl. There is therefore nothing to discuss.

Reina is a bit too normal as well.

Miu talks herself up too much for my liking.

Haruka is your normal bar owner so far. Only thing we know about her is her husband is at war. I actually feel bad for the husband, knowing that she is being unfaithful, and dislike Haruka a bit more due to that.

For similar reasons as Haruka, Sara is not really that nice of an individual. It feels like every female that is out of high school just ended up being unfaithful. Nice for the guy at the center of the harem, but that means you can never trust them... or really like them much.

Kaori is a rather nice individual. Not sure how she is able to work in so many places, I guess we will need more plot to find out about her. Hope to not find out that she is interested in sex and yet is cheating on her boyfriend.

Kirin and Karin are decent side characters. Kirin is the better sister as she promised sex and showed her panties on our first meeting with her. Karen didn't really do anything sexual with us.

Chinami seems dangerously close to getting people on the FBI's watch list. She already talked about white vans...

Maki looks oddly like Yumi...

Saki is an extremely loyal being who is willing to spend all of time with you. She enjoys whales, which are rather gentle animals, plus always has a good supply of candy on hand when nobody else seems to be feeding you. She is the only one who seems to come over if we do not go outside. She is the only one who was there when nobody else was. She is the only one who genuinely loves you. The only one who will be there until you die. Then will be with your corpse. The only one who knows Josh is alive outside of us. I feel like the rest of the world has ignored Josh for far too long. It is Josh's time to shine, Josh's story to tell.

61 6d 20 69 20 6f 6b 61 79 just ends up rambling about her interests too much for my liking. She stopped conversing with me after my niece showed up, which I felt was rather rude. She also had sex with a machine and mocked me. The fact that she doesn't have sex with me prevents her from being a redemptive character, though I do feel she could master backwards spider crawl if she just let me get closer to her.

Hope is a wonderful being that seems rather curious as to my presence, of to which I am quite grateful. I for one love people who are interested in me. That probably sounds conceited. Ah well, you don't exist anyway. Anyway, I am looking forward to further developments on the Hope route. Combined with the fact that Hope has a small harem of angels with easy to remember names (always a plus to any harem, since harems with people who have names that are hard to remember will always make daily living more complicated) I currently feel that Hope is the best girl in Lessons of Love even if they have yet to get a proper route. But that is okay! You promised everyone would be given a route in time, and Hope, much like myself, is probably a patient being.

spoilers.title: Impressions
spoilers.html:
Needless to say, I am not exactly the normal person here. Most came for the girls, stayed for the horror, I came for the horror and fell in love with the comedy and stories. This game is definitely one of the best VNs I know, mainly because of the ties to English. I definitely see what people mean by this game being somewhat similar to Doki Doki. The resetting of the world probably didn't help things there, plus it is what people think of when they think glitchy content. If I had to compare the two, I would say this game works a bit better, even with the horror element. Doki Doki had some flickering and suicidal scenes, but it never had things like Yumi's park scene or MS paint insanity.

The hidden scenes aren't just little surprises, they are some of the biggest attractions for me. They feel like a great period where you can let your creativity free and just let insanity in the door. It gets intriguing just how wild you will make the scenes and what exactly is going to occur. So far they have been quite nice to blunder across; so far I have naturally worked the routes in such a way that the scenes happened to occur when you least expected them. I will say that the new one for 5.0 is perhaps one of the best yet; it gave me a Cartagra vibe in what I felt was one of the best sequences of the game (Takako route).

Of course, the big thing of 5.0 is the words "everything is connected". After running through all the content, it is more true than ever, and I am quite glad I did things in the manner I did them. Perhaps it was just a side nod to Nothing is Beautiful... but what if it was something more? What if Yuu is Sensei? All paths intertwined. A million memories in the same place. What if this is Yuu's chance to live... a life that could be lived simply by jumping. A life where you no longer had to take candy or stay in the same place. A life where things are buried under the school and nobody looks for them because everybody is happy.

spoilers.title: The Girls
spoilers.html:
If I had to say a route I particularly am interested in, which is hard given that this game so far has you working all routes sort of simultaneously, I would say Yumi. It is probably the furthest interest from love I would have, since I absolutely dislike tsunderes and get more aggressive towards them (is it wrong that I cheered her being traumatized? Probably. But nothing is real). However, her reactions to Sensei following her around everywhere and the impromptu ska music works rather well. It makes it a rather fun read, even if I hate her as a person. I bet you hate many people too. All those people will be dead one day. You likely will be dead by then as well though.

Based on my tastes, I should probably be leaning towards the Sana route. The quiet shy character always seems alluring to me, perhaps because I am rather introverted. The leaning to escapism to avoid pain, the dissolution of the tangible threads around you as you embrace worlds far more interesting. If nothing is real, everything is equally relative, and thus all worlds are worlds to experience and place value in. However, she seems somewhat lacking in embracing darkness, instead playing Animal Crossing and seeking to improve herself.

Rin has that darkness I prefer, though she is far more punk rock than gothic or metal like I rather. She is also extremely social in ways that almost seem exhausting if done for too long. She could be a good wing-man though and a somewhat good friend. She seems genuinely interested in trying to get me with where I should be, so I must say that is a pretty welcoming quality to have in a friend. Plus being bisexual means that she can gauge my interests more, needed for a proper wingman.

Ayane isn't really a character I can say is attractive physically. Never been one for blonde hair. She manages to overcome this handicap with eccentric tastes that intrigue me, I enjoy the unpredictable and thus it is quite appealing to see what she will pull up. Plus we are on F95, someone that willingly is that perverted is a massive plus. Not sure how I feel about her tastes on pop music, but at least there is one girl who would willingly do anything sexual.

Ami just reminds me of Emi from Katawa Shoujo. Not only does she have a similar name and have a similar extroverted personality, but she also has dead parents. She, like the clone of her before her, fall into the category of being somewhat alright while also being nothing standout. Maybe Ami should do something different like murder someone. Maybe she should murder all the other girls and then finger herself to their corpses? Much better than just being a girl with dead parents.

Makoto is quite the competition for Ami in the "I don't really hate you but also don't really care you exist" category. It is a category reserved for most people and thus is one that isn't really that special or interesting. Thus I wouldn't be surprised if I was in a similar category for most people! Day 1

-[Irrelevant Van Halen reference in my mind when Jump appeared]
-*screaming internally at the "static" and translating the hexadecimal*
-I need to stop. It's late... *keeps going*

Day 2
-Perfectly normal harem game, let's visit my niece!
-Hang on this isn't my niece's room, this is a room with clocks!!
-I'm not crying during this scene with clocks because I'm caught off guard, you are.
-Normal...normal...normal *still on the edge of my seat*
-More existential crisis!
-"Are you happy?" Hmm...I have a choice to say I'm miserable? Let's see what happens when I click- NOPE NOPE NOPE NOPE!
-I'm happy and this game is normal! *panic*

Day 3
-Oh, I just realized there is a Missing event. *screams internally*
-Ok more smut.
-What's this smiley face?
-This game knows it is torturing me and is ok with it. I'm ok with this as well.

Overall review from what I have played: 15/10, More please! I like how this gives me heavy DDLC vibes. Selebus, you have exceeded my expectations and I want more. I am not usually a horror fan but this is fantastic. Keep it up!

posts.content_html_raw:
Maaaan this was a really wholesome update. Is it just me or both Maya and Yumi are showing a softer side lately? I feel particularly less insulted at every turn in this update.
Also, I feel like the "happy" factor took a step back, which was surprising in an update so filled with Maya events. Somehow the Haruka conversation stuck out more for me than the main dish this update. Really interesting stuff with her.

But what stuck out for me the most this update were the heartwarming moments with Futaba, Miku, Rin and Yumi.

With Yumi was a blink and miss it, but Sensei showing concern about her well-being making her smile was fantastic. She knows we are scumbags, but we are genuine in the whole helping her out part.
That moment shared with Miku showing us" her world" was great as well. Somehow she is climbing the "want to protect" ranks.
Rin is such a lovable character. Probably the one I would want to help the most irl. That hint of liking us along Chika helped subside the fear of the impact for when she finds out Chika has her sights on us. Really, for the love of 4e 6f 7a 6f 6d 75, don't let US break her heart.
Still, the most heartwarming moment prize this update is taken by Futaba's confession. Or rather Sensei's response to her. I think this was the one event that showed his character's growth. This is it. His one opportunity to being happy and not just "happy" is trying to help these girls. The H content is just a bonus.

TL;DR: The creepy factor was somehow toned down this time to grant some wholesome character developments, which I welcome. I think this was a perfect balance of both aspects to this story.

posts.content_html_raw:
Kaato said:
Hey can anyone fill me on the horror factors in this game. If you can go into detail then please do. Im not the horror type guy. After I got my first secret event... well you know how it went. I'd atleast like some assurance. As much as I want to play game, my mind just won't let me.
Click to expand...
What you got is pretty much what you will keep seeing.
At the beginning is pretty prominent depending of how you quickly play each storyline, but there is plenty of fluff and wholesome stuff to balance it out. I think the "horror" in a few "jumpscares" (most being really telegraphed and seen miles away to prepare your heart) is worth the great story underneath each girl.

I just keep playing the game with the hope of MC developing and slowly helping the girls with the issues (which in exchange will help him themselves)

I think the biggest factor in the "horror" aren't these few quirky "jumpscares" though. Its more psychological, with heavy messages about humans, relationships, happiness, life... and all its counterparts. God, loneliness, sadness and death.

I strongly recommend that you try tough it up and go through with it. Its totally worth it.
